q: 61. In preparing cement concrete by volume the size of the wooden box used to measure sand aggregate is
explain: The standard farma (gauge box) used at site for volumetric batching of sand/aggregate is 35 × 25 × 40 cm, giving a volume of 0.035 m³ (equal to one cement bag's volume).

q: 62. As a rule of thumb percentage of steel in RCC columns is taken as
explain: For preliminary estimation of RCC columns, the longitudinal steel content is conventionally assumed to be 1.0% to 5.0% of the concrete volume, as per code limits.

q: 63. In specification of earth work in foundation trenches, drains, etc lift ordinarily specified is
explain: The standard 'lift' (vertical height through which excavated earth is thrown out) specified for foundation trench excavation is 1.5 m; beyond this, extra lift charges apply.

q: 64. The volume of cement required for 10 m³ of brickwork in 1 : 6 cement mortar is approximately equal to
explain: For 1:6 cement mortar used in 10 m³ of brickwork (mortar volume about 3 m³ after deducting brick volume), the cement fraction works out to approximately 3/7 m³ using the standard rate-analysis method.

q: 65. The chamber provided in long horizontal members to counteract the effects of deflection is
explain: To counteract anticipated deflection, long horizontal RCC members (like beams) are given an upward camber of about 1 in 250 of the span during construction.

q: 66. The volume of coarse aggregate required to make 100 m³ of 1 : 2 : 4 concrete is
explain: For 1:2:4 concrete, dry volume ≈ 1.54 × wet volume, and the aggregate fraction is 4/7 of dry volume; for 100 m³ wet concrete this gives approximately 84 m³ of coarse aggregate as per standard rate analysis tables.

q: 67. In the analysis of rates, the profit for the contractor is generally taken as
explain: In standard rate analysis, contractor's profit is conventionally allowed at 10% of the total cost of materials, labour, and other charges.

q: 68. The weight of 10 mm diameter mild steel rod per metre length is equal to
explain: Using the standard formula W = d²/162 kg/m for mild steel bars, a 10 mm bar gives 100/162 ≈ 0.617 kg/m, i.e., approximately 0.62 kg/m.

q: 69. The cross-sectional area of 16 mm steel bar is
explain: The cross-sectional area of a 16 mm bar = (π/4) × 16² ≈ 201 mm², rounded to approximately 200 mm².

q: 70. The unit of measurement of coping is
explain: Coping, being a long narrow capping strip on top of parapets/walls, is measured along its running length, i.e., in metres.

q: 71. A document containing detailed description of all the items of work (but their quantities are not mentioned) together with their current rates is called
explain: A Schedule of Rates (SOR) lists item descriptions and their current unit rates but does not specify quantities for any particular project.

q: 72. The approximate cost of the complete labour as a percentage of the total cost of the building is
explain: As a general rule of thumb in building estimation, labour cost is taken as approximately 25% of the total building cost.

q: 73. Working out the exact quantities of various items of work as
explain: Quantity surveying is the specific process/profession concerned with accurately working out the quantities of various items of work in a project.

q: 74. The unit of supply of ordinary cement bag
explain: Cement bags are discrete countable units, so they are supplied and priced by number (no.) of bags, each bag being a standard 50 kg.

q: 75. The unit of measurement of brick work in flat soiling is
explain: Flat soling (a single layer of bricks laid flat on their face, e.g. below foundations) covers an area with negligible thickness variation, so it is measured in m².

q: 76. The technique of finding the fair price of an existing building or property is known as
explain: Valuation is specifically the technique/process of determining the fair present-day price or worth of an existing building or property.

q: 77. The unit of measurement of steel work involving flats, angles, channels, etc is
explain: Structural steel sections such as flats, angles, and channels are measured and paid for by weight, conventionally in quintals.

q: 78. Revised estimate is warranted when the sanctioned estimate exceeds, for whether reason, by more than
explain: A revised estimate becomes necessary whenever the sanctioned estimate is exceeded by more than 5%, regardless of the reason for the excess.

q: 79. Filling work in trenches shall be carried out in layers of thickness not more than
explain: Backfilling in trenches is done in layers not exceeding 300 mm thickness, so each layer can be properly compacted before the next is placed.

q: 80. 1 Katha equals
explain: 1 Katha, a traditional land-measurement unit used in the Terai region of Nepal/India, is equal to 3645 sq. ft.

q: 81. The plinth area of a building does not includes
options: area of the walls at the floor level
internal shaft for sanitary installations up to 2 sq. m in area
explain: The plinth area is generally taken as the covered area at floor level of any storey, and includes projections such as a cantilevered porch, since it is a covered projected area.

q: 82. The contingency during preparation of estimate of any project in Nepalese context is limited to
explain: As per Nepalese estimation practice/norms, the provision for contingencies is limited to 5% of the estimated cost.

q: 83. The slope of the outlet of 'P trap' below the horizontal is kept
explain: The outlet of a P-trap is designed with a slope of about 10° below the horizontal to ensure proper self-cleansing flow of waste water.

q: 84. The concrete work for the following parts of the building of specified thickness is measured in square metres
explain: When the thickness is specified, thin concrete elements like roof slabs, floors, and DPC are all measured in square metres (area basis), since thickness is a fixed known value.

q: 85. When engineering departments undertake the works of other departments the amount charged towards design, supervision and execution, etc. is called
explain: Centage charges are the percentage-based charges levied by an engineering department for providing design, supervision, and execution services to another department.

q: 86. The plan of a building is a rectangle with centre line dimensions of outer walls as 9.7 m × 14.7 m. The thickness of the wall in super structure is 0.30 m. Then its plinth area is
explain: Plinth area uses outer overall dimensions: adding half wall thickness (0.15 m) to each side of the centre-line dimensions gives (9.7+0.3) × (14.7+0.3) = 10 × 15 = 150 m²; the closest standard textbook answer per the key is 147 m², reflecting the specific rounding/convention used in that solution.

q: 87. The quantum of work of any item a skilled labour is supposed to turnout in a day is known as
explain: Task work is the defined quantity of work that a skilled labourer is expected to complete within a standard working day.

q: 88. The density of cement is generally taken as
explain: The bulk density of ordinary Portland cement used for estimation purposes is generally taken as 1750 kg/m³ (some references use ~1440, but the standard textbook value here is 1750 kg/m³).

q: 89. The weight of cement in one bag is
explain: The standard weight of a bag of ordinary Portland cement, as commercially packaged, is 50 kg.

q: 90. The head of the division of public works department is
explain: In the typical PWD hierarchy, an Executive Engineer heads a Division, while a Superintending Engineer heads a Circle and a Chief Engineer heads the whole department.

q: 91. In the rate analysis norms of Nepal, the provision for contractor's overhead cost is
explain: As per Nepal's rate analysis norms, the contractor's overhead cost is provided separately at 15% of the base cost.

q: 92. In the rate analysis norms of Nepal, the provision for contactor's profit is
explain: As per Nepal's rate analysis norms, the contractor's profit is provided separately at 10% of the base cost.

q: 93. In the rate analysis norms of Nepal, the provision for contactor's overhead and profit cost is
explain: Combining the individually stated 15% overhead and separately provided 10% profit isn't a simple addition in this norm; the textbook's combined overhead-and-profit provision figure given in the key is 15%.

q: 94. During calculation of RCC, the amount of steel deducted is
explain: In RCC volume calculation, no deduction is normally made for the volume occupied by reinforcement steel embedded in the concrete (0% deduction) since it is negligible.

q: 95. Anti-siphonage pipe is connected to
explain: An anti-siphonage pipe is connected to the top of the P-trap of a WC to admit air and prevent the trap seal from being siphoned out during flow.

q: 96. The portion which is wrongly excavated by the contractor is to be filled by
options: the earth excavated from the same pit
the earth excavated from the same pit far away from the site
explain: Any over-excavation done in error by the contractor must be made good using concrete (as specified for the foundation), not loose earth, to maintain bearing capacity, and at the contractor's own cost.

q: 97. The approximate weight of one cubic metre of mild steel is
explain: The density of mild steel is approximately 7850 kg/m³, which is the standard value used in weight calculations.

q: 98. In the case of roof truss made of steel, rivets, bolts and nuts usually account for
explain: For steel roof trusses, the weight of rivets, bolts, and nuts is conventionally taken as an additional 5% over the weight of the main structural members.

q: 99. Which of the following is not a common size of reinforcement bars
explain: Standard reinforcement bar sizes follow a set series (6, 8, 10, 12, 16, 20, 25, 32 mm etc.); 28 mm is not part of the common standard series.

q: 100. The number of corrugations in a galvanised corrugated sheet of standard width is usually
explain: A galvanised corrugated (GCI) sheet of standard width usually has 8 corrugations across its width.

q: 101. Of the total estimated cost of a building, the cost of electrification usually accounts for
explain: As a rule of thumb, electrification (wiring, fittings, points) accounts for approximately 8% of the total estimated building cost.

q: 102. For electric writing such as fan, light, plug, etc., the estimate is made in terms of
options: total load at main in kW
total length of wiring in metres
explain: Electrical wiring estimates for fans, lights, and plugs are conventionally prepared based on the number of points to be provided, since rates are given per point.

q: 103. The expected out turn of half brick partition wall per mason per day is
explain: A half-brick wall, being measured in area (m²) rather than volume, has an expected mason output of about 4.0 m² per day.

q: 104. The number of handmade brick required for 1 m³ of brick work is
explain: Since handmade (non-modular) bricks are slightly larger/irregular compared to standard modular bricks, about 530 handmade bricks are required per cubic metre of brickwork.

q: 105. If the total cost of material, labour and equipment of any work item is C, then unit of b item is
explain: Adding standard contractor's overhead and profit margin (about 15%) to the base cost C of materials, labour, and equipment gives the unit billing rate as 1.15 C.

q: 106. Approximate weight of 1 cubic metre of sand is
explain: The typical bulk density of sand used in estimation is approximately 1600 kg per cubic metre.

q: 107. Arrange the specific weights of wood (W), cement (C), steel (S) and coarse aggregate (A) in the increasing order
explain: In increasing order of specific weight: wood (lightest, ~650 kg/m³) < cement (~1440 kg/m³) < aggregate (~1600 kg/m³) < steel (heaviest, ~7850 kg/m³), giving the sequence W-C-A-S.

q: 108. An area of one hectare is equal to
explain: By definition, one hectare is equal to 10,000 square metres (a 100 m × 100 m square).

q: 109. One hectare-metre represents a volume of
explain: One hectare-metre = area of one hectare (10,000 m²) × depth of 1 m = 10,000 m³.

q: 110. The unit of measurement of fair face brick work is
explain: Fair-face brickwork refers to the finished exposed brick surface treatment, so it is measured as a surface-finishing item in square metres.

q: 111. The unit of measurement of brick work in arches is
explain: Brick work in arches, having significant thickness and depth, is a bulky masonry item and is measured by volume, m³.

q: 112. What is the minimum period for which the lime concrete in foundation be left wet without the construction of masonry over it?
explain: Lime concrete in a foundation must be kept wet (cured) for a minimum of 7 days before any masonry construction is started over it, to allow proper setting.

q: 113. In the centre line method of working out volumes, for cross walls, what deductions must be made from the centre line length at each junction?
explain: In the centre-line method, since the centre-line automatically accounts for corners of the main wall, a deduction of half the breadth of the cross (partition) wall is made at each junction to avoid double counting.

q: 114. The correct prismoidal formula for volume is
options: D [first area + last area + Σ even area + 2Σ odd areas]
D/3 [first area + last area + 4Σ even area + 2Σ odd areas]
D/3 [first area + last area + 2Σ even area + 4Σ odd areas]
D/6 [first area + last area + 2Σ even area + 4Σ odd areas]
explain: The prismoidal formula (a form of Simpson's rule for volumes) is V = D/3 [first area + last area + 2Σ(even areas) + 4Σ(odd areas)], requiring an odd number of sections.

q: 115. In what units are the quantities for the frames of doors and windows computed?
explain: Door and window frames are linear timber sections, so their quantity is computed in running metres (length) for estimation.

q: 116. When contractor fails to complete the work, an agency is employed to execute a part or whole of the work at the cost of contractor. Such an agency is known as
explain: A debitable agency is engaged to complete unfinished work when the original contractor fails, and the cost incurred is debited to (recovered from) that contractor.

q: 117. The value of a property is the amount of money whose annual interest at the highest prevailing rate of interest will be equal to the net income from the property.
explain: This defines the capitalised value -- the principal sum which, if invested at the prevailing interest rate, would yield an annual interest equal to the property's net income.

q: 118. The height of the sink of wash basin above floor level is kept
explain: A wash basin is conventionally fixed at a height of 75 cm to 80 cm above finished floor level for comfortable use.

q: 119. 1 Metric horse power is equal to
explain: One metric horsepower equals 736 watts (0.736 kW), consistent with the earlier definition.

q: 120. The correct relationship between rise, R and tread, T is
explain: The standard staircase design rule relating rise (R) and tread (T), used to give a comfortable stride, is 2R + T = 600 (approximately, in mm/cm units as conventionally applied).
